thread.title: Airbus Executive Says Progress on A320neo, Hints at A350 Output Rise

title: Airbus Executive Says Progress on A320neo, Hints at A350 Output Rise
text:
Airbus Executive Says Progress on A320neo, Hints at A350 Output Rise Feb. 20, 2018, at 9:09 a.m. Airbus Executive Says Progress on A320neo, Hints at A350 Output Rise Share FILE PHOTO: The logo of Airbus is pictured during Airbus annual press conference on the 2017 financial results in Blagnac near Toulouse, France, February 15, 2018. REUTERS/Regis Duvignau Reuters 
TOULOUSE, France (Reuters) - Airbus said it was making good progress in resolving Pratt & Whitney engine snags that are holding up some A320neo narrowbody deliveries, and gave a fresh signal it is considering raising output of its larger A350 wide-body jet. 
Programmes Chief Didier Evrard told reporters on Tuesday that the supply chain could cope with more than 10 A350 deliveries a month, the current target Airbus aims to reach by the year-end. 
He was speaking on the sidelines of the inaugural delivery of the largest version of the jet, the A350-1000, to launch customer Qatar Airways. 
(Reporting by Alexander CornwellWriting by Tim HepherEditing by Sudip Kar-Gupta)
